company.description: Company name, also used in the salutation.

role.description: Job title as published, used in the subject.

place.description: Place for the date line. Defaults to applicant.currentCity without the country.

age.description: Age used in 'I’m a XX-year-old'. Fixed in PERSONAL; override only on explicit request.

job_title.description: Title used in 'I’m a ...'. Usually the target role or your current level. Optional override; normally fixed in PERSONAL in render.py.

years_experience.description: Total software-development years, used in 'with over ... years of experience developing and maintaining complex enterprise software'.

backend_scope.description: What you want to take care of, after 'take care of your'.

product.description: The company product/platform, after 'sustainable success of your'.

match_reason.default: I believe we’re a match because

current_company.description: After 'In my current position with'. Optional override; normally fixed in PERSONAL in render.py.

achievement.description: After 'I have ...'. Use a past-tense verb phrase. Optional override; normally fixed in PERSONAL in render.py.

previous_work.description: After 'Before that I was ...'. Use a gerund phrase, e.g. designing and building. Optional override; normally fixed in PERSONAL in render.py.

strength_1.default: bring a profound understanding of the entire delivery pipeline

start_date.description: After 'starting'. Optional override; normally fixed in PERSONAL in render.py.

fill_header.description: Fill the non-highlighted recipient block, date and signature. Set false to keep the template's literal Company/Street/City/Place/Firstname Lastname lines.

highlight_fields.description: Optional list of field names to highlight in yellow in the output. Used only to build the base template; final letters leave it empty.

tech_points.description: 2-3 named technologies extracted from the JD that also appear in the CV, e.g. 'React and TypeScript' or 'React, TypeScript and Node.js'. No more than 3. Each item must be a concrete language, framework, library, runtime, database or cloud service. Never use categories or work areas: 'component libraries', 'frameworks', 'design systems', 'frontend', 'backend', 'tools' are not technologies.

non_tech_1.description: First non-technical strength extracted from the JD, e.g. 'clean, maintainable code' or 'technical ownership'.

non_tech_2.description: Second non-technical strength extracted from the JD, e.g. 'reliable delivery' or 'cross-functional collaboration'.
